Order evidence

Signatures verify the signer and order bytes. They do not attest to Coinbase’s reference data or establish on-chain finality.

UNDER THE HOOD

What’s real here?

Actual SDK execution

The unchanged Rust CLOB matcher, SDK transaction format, signing and verification run in your browser as WebAssembly. The office visualizes this session.

Live references. Paper trades.

BTC, ETH, SOL and USDC USD spot references come from Coinbase’s public API, refreshed every 10 seconds. Paper quotes sit around those references with illustrative spreads. These fills are not exchange orders or guaranteed spot-price executions. Trading pauses if references are over 45 seconds old.

Office and candlesticks

Both camera views share a wider physical monitor. The main chart shows Coinbase market candles and volume in USD, refreshed every minute. The spot reference updates every 10 seconds. Expand it for readable prices, crosshairs, zoom and 1m, 5m or 1h intervals. The adjacent order book is SDK paper liquidity in USDC. The advanced terminal keeps its separate three-fill paper execution candles. Walkthrough pacing is educational, not a latency benchmark.

Application rules around the SDK

The bots follow scripts. Paper BTC, ETH, SOL and USDC have no value. This application implements shared balances, reservations, settlement, self-trade rejection and signed cancellations around the matcher. There is no deployed validator network or consensus finality. All signing keys are public demo keys.
